head.title: What’s new in Higgsfield: releases, improvements, and fixes
head.description: Follow the latest Higgsfield product updates, improvements, and releases.
head.og_title: What’s new in Higgsfield: releases, improvements, and fixes
head.author: Higgsfield.AI Team

entries.title: Editing Room
entries.summary: Higgsfield Editing Room is a video-to-video editor: swap the person, angle, location, camera move, or lighting in any moment of your own footage.
entries.content:
A video-to-video editor for your own footage: upload a clip, pick any moment, and swap the person, angle, location, camera move, or lighting in one place.

Edits apply only to the selected moment and stack on each other, so a new angle can get a camera move and then new lighting without re-uploading.

  • Tools: Swap person, Change angle, Change location, Move camera, Relight, and Edit with brush, where you paint over an area and describe the change.
  • Timeline: split a shot with Cut here, mark a moment on the lane above it and adjust its edges.
  • Relight: presets, custom light sources with direction, color, brightness, and diffusion, or a text description.
  • Review: several edits can run at once; compare each with the original in Split or Compare view, then export the finished video.

To get started: open Editing Room → Upload your video → mark a moment → choose a tool → Generate.

entries.title: Ideogram 4.6
entries.summary: Ideogram 4.6 is now on Higgsfield: step-by-step image edits designed to change only what you ask, up to 5 references, and native 4K output.
entries.content:
Ideogram’s new image model is now on Higgsfield, built for precise editing.

It’s designed to change only what you ask for, so a product color, a material, or a background can be swapped one change at a time while the face, details, and composition stay in place, per Ideogram.

  • Step-by-step edits: each edit builds on the previous one.
  • References: up to 5 per generation.
  • Resolution: 2K or native 4K, without upscaling; Very low quality is limited to 2K.
  • Quality: Very low, Low, Medium, or High.

To get started: Image → Ideogram 4.6 → Generate.

entries.title: Property Studio
entries.summary: Property Studio on Higgsfield turns a floor plan into a furnished 3D layout and a narrated video tour, for real estate agents, developers, and designers.
entries.content:
A real estate tool that turns a floor plan into a furnished 3D layout and a narrated video tour you can share.

It’s built for agents, developers, and interior designers. The result is a visualization based on the plan.

  • Floor plan: rooms are recognized and labeled automatically; add renders or references for each room, or one style for all of them, up to 20 images.
  • 3D layout: walls and then furniture are built step by step; walk into any room and describe changes in text.
  • Script and voice: a room-by-room script is written for you to edit, regenerate, or replace, then narrated by a library voice, your own voice from a short sample, or a ready recording.
  • Video: preview the tour, adjust it, and generate the final version.

To get started: open Property Studio → upload a floor plan → follow the steps through 3D Layout, Script & voice, and Video.

entries.title: Gemini 4 Neon
entries.summary: Gemini 4 Neon from Google is now in Higgsfield Supercomputer: a language model for code, documents, and analysis with a 1M-token context.
entries.content:
Google’s new language model for code, documents, and analysis is now in Supercomputer on Higgsfield.

It fits tasks too complex for Hydrogen, which is built for quick everyday work, that still don’t need Carbon, which handles the most demanding long-running projects.

Per Google:

  • Code: sites, apps, games, and 3D, with edits across several files in large projects.
  • Documents and data: reads spreadsheets, PDFs, charts, photos, audio, and video, and turns them into reports and summaries, with a context of up to 1M tokens.
  • Analysis: calculations, research, and multi-step math and science tasks.
  • Corrections: adjusts course when you redirect it mid-task.

To get started: open Supercomputer → select Gemini 4 Neon.

entries.title: Kling Image 4.0
entries.summary: Kling Image 4.0 is now on Higgsfield: photoreal images up to 8K, up to 2,000 characters of text in 7 languages, and series of 10 images from one prompt.
entries.content:
Kling’s new image model is now on Higgsfield, generating from text and references.

It’s aimed at photoreal portraits and group shots, and at designs with a lot of text, such as posters, infographics, and product cards.

Per Kling:

  • Realism: designed for natural light and skin and material texture.
  • Text: up to 2,000 characters per image in 7 languages, with 70+ fonts or a font matched from a reference.
  • Prompts: up to 15,000 tokens, enough for a detailed brief on layout and composition.
  • Series: up to 10 images in one style from a single prompt.
  • Resolution: 2K by default, 4K, or 8K.

To get started: Image → Kling Image 4.0 → Generate.

entries.title: Linked billing for Claude in Supercomputer
entries.summary: Claude API usage in Higgsfield Supercomputer can now be billed by Anthropic to your Claude Platform organization. Beta for Team, Scale, and Enterprise.
entries.content:
Claude API usage in Supercomputer can now be billed by Anthropic directly to your own Claude Platform organization.

Linked billing is in beta, with Higgsfield among Anthropic’s launch partners. Image and video generations still use Higgsfield credits.

  • No shared keys: the link is approved on the Claude side by an Owner, Admin, or Billing administrator of the organization.
  • Spending control: usage, monthly limits, and unlinking are managed in Claude Console.

To get started: Manage Account → Workspace settings → Claude → Link your Claude organization → approve the connection in Claude → check that the status shows Linked.

Availability: Team, Scale, and Enterprise plans.

entries.title: GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol
entries.summary: GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol from OpenAI are now in Higgsfield Supercomputer: a flagship for complex projects and a lower-cost model for everyday work.
entries.content:
OpenAI’s two new language models are now in Supercomputer on Higgsfield: a flagship for complex projects and a lower-cost model for everyday work.

Sol is a good pick for most tasks, while Astra is a better choice for large, demanding work like template-based decks and full builds.

Per OpenAI:

  • Astra: documents, spreadsheets, and slides that follow a template down to layout, colors, and fonts, plus cleaner code for sites, games, and 3D.
  • Sol: multi-step agentic tasks and natural writing; on FrontierCode 2.0 it scores within 0.5 points of Astra at about a fifth of the cost.
  • Efficiency: better results on complex tasks with fewer tokens than the previous versions.

To get started: open Supercomputer → select GPT-6.2 Astra or GPT-6.2 Sol.

entries.title: Short Drama Studio
entries.summary: Higgsfield Short Drama Studio turns a script into a short series: episodes, a consistent cast, and locations generated from your text in 15 styles. Early preview.
entries.content:
A studio that turns a script into a short series: it splits the text into episodes, builds the cast, locations, and props, and generates the episodes with the same characters throughout.

It’s in early preview, available on desktop only for now.

  • Script: PDF, DOCX, FDX, TXT, or MD up to 10 MB; six aspect ratios and 15 styles, from Higgsfield Cinematic and K-Drama to Anime and Classic 3D.
  • Cast & World: characters, locations, and props are generated from the text.
  • Episodes: each one is planned into scenes and clips, then generated at 480p draft, 720p, or 1080p.
  • Ways to work: step by step, Auto-generate all with one set of settings, or through the Agent panel in chat.

To get started: open Short Drama → upload a script → pick a format and style → Analyze script or Auto-generate all. In Claude, connect Higgsfield MCP and ask for a short drama.

Availability: early preview on the desktop version, and in Claude through Higgsfield MCP.
